gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-tifina: Noto Sans Tifinagh swells into rounded, inflated bowls that fill the line. Bushcraft sits over it with closed, widely spaced letters, one weight all the way round, so the heading looks like cord and the body looks like breath.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-tirhut: Bushcraft lays out rounded, cord-like strokes with extra space between every character. Noto Sans Tirhuta follows with a dominant x-height and terminals cut back to leave big gaps, so a long page would feel contemporary and easy to move through.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-ugarit: Noto Sans Ugaritic keeps its lowercase close to cap height, with open mouths like unjoined chalk arcs, which gives text a friendly, compact look. Bushcraft's stems and arches are identical in thickness above it, so enlarge only the body if it feels tight.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-vai: Noto Sans Vai makes words read as solid blocks rather than skylines, with generous space between curve ends and stems. Bushcraft, with no hairline anywhere, loosens up the heading while the body holds the page together.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-vithku: Expressive lettering leads here, spaced wide and closed. Noto Sans Vithkuqi follows with open throats on a, c, e and s, and only a minimal step from capitals down to lowercase, so a long page reads smoothly beneath Bushcraft.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Artistic and wire-thin in its skeleton, Bushcraft hands off to Noto Sans Wancho, a hulking lowercase pressed down like thick chalk with a wide gap in the e. That weight gap is the strongest thing here.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-warang: Words in Noto Sans Warang Citi form solid blocks, with wide channels leading into each counter. Bushcraft gives the heading closed letters and curves that turn corners without any pressure swell, so the two feel like rope beside open water.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-yi: Bushcraft builds its heading from rounded rods in a single weight, with closed letters and generous spacing, and that is where it does its best work. Noto Sans Yi does its best in the body, with a deep midsection and rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-zanaba: Bushcraft stretches out expressive, closed letters with extra space between each one, and no capital pushes far above the lowercase. Noto Sans Zanabazar Square lifts a soaring x-height beside it, crisp and open.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-traditional: Approachable and broad-nibbed, Noto Traditional Nushu never lets a stroke curl shut. Its bowls fill the line, so a long passage under the closed, spaced-out Bushcraft would read in a steady, friendly flow.
